Only the toddler build is choking-safe for under-3s; popcorn, raisins, stamp heads, game parts and coin batteries belong in older children's baskets only.

faqs.question: Which items go in a kids' boo basket?
faqs.answer: Five to seven items matched to one age band: something to wear or use, something to do, one treat and a note. Toddlers get large, soft items with no hard sweets; tweens and teens get things they choose, such as a film rental or a voucher.

faqs.question: How much does a boo basket for kids cost?
faqs.answer: The seven builds on this page are estimated at US$20 to US$70, at rounded mid-range shop prices. The no-food and preschool baskets sit at the low end; the sibling pair costs most because every item is doubled.

faqs.question: Is a boo basket safe for a toddler?
faqs.answer: Only if every item is too large to choke on and there are no hard sweets, nuts, popcorn or coin batteries. The toddler build here uses a towel, bath cups, a hand puppet, a spoon set, a sealed night light and a purée pouch for that reason.

faqs.question: When should I give a boo basket to a child?
faqs.answer: Early October gives the most use. Halloween is Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027, so a basket left on the first weekend of October gives about four weeks.

faqs.question: Can I boo my neighbour's kids without asking?
faqs.answer: Ask a parent first. One message tells you about allergies and whether the family celebrates Halloween, and it stops a stranger's basket from worrying anyone.

faqs.question: What is a good boo basket for a 10-year-old?
faqs.answer: A horror-lite movie night: a PG-rated film they pick, popcorn, a dark beanie and a 10+ puzzle game. Skip cartoon pumpkins, which read as babyish at that age.

faqs.question: How do I make a boo basket for two siblings?
faqs.answer: Use two baskets with the same number of items, in two colours, plus one item that needs both children, such as a walkie-talkie pair. If one child is under 3, box the older child's small parts.

faqs.question: What is a non-candy boo basket for a child with allergies?
faqs.answer: Leave out food entirely: paints and paper, gloves, a water bottle, a cape and a film coupon. Check modelling dough labels, because many doughs contain wheat.

faqs.question: Does the US small-parts rule cover Halloween pyjamas and hair clips?
faqs.answer: No. 16 CFR 1501 covers toys and articles for children under 3, and its exemption list includes children's clothing and accessories such as buttons, plus barrettes, books, crayons, clay and paints. You have to check their size yourself.

faqs.question: Can grandparents far away send something for the basket?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Halloween page in its Kids setting can travel as a link and serve as the note; it keeps the ghosts cute and skips every scare. The premium page lets a grandparent record a short voice message, a minute at most.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Boo Basket for Kids: 7 Builds by Age, With Choking Flags

A boo basket for kids works when it holds five to seven items picked for one age band, with nothing a child under 3 could choke on if a toddler lives in the house. Below are seven complete builds, from age 1 to 17, each flagged for choking risk, priced as an estimate and timed to assemble.

For the note inside, a link travels well: nearly half (48.3%) of the SubhSandesh pages people share get opened on phones, and 90.9% of started pages reach publishing. After the builds: the small-parts rule, neighbour etiquette and what a child study says about polite thanks.

## What is a boo basket for kids?

A boo basket for kids is a small Halloween gift basket, left for a child during October, holding a handful of seasonal treats and things to do. It is closer to an Easter basket than to a party favour bag, because it is built for one child rather than for a crowd.

Give it early. With Halloween landing on a Saturday in 2026 (31 October) and a Sunday in 2027 (31 October), a basket left on the first October weekend gives four weeks of use.

## 7 boo basket builds for kids, from age 1 to 17

Each build lists items, choking flag, estimated cost and assembly time, in that order. Costs are rounded US-dollar estimates at mid-range shop prices and vary by country.

### 1. Toddler, ages 1 to 3: bath-night pumpkin

Bath time is when toddlers are watched most closely, which makes it the safest place for new things. Nothing here is food except one soft pouch.

- A pumpkin-orange hooded towel
- Three nesting bath cups, each wider than a child's fist
- A ghost hand puppet that covers an adult's whole hand
- A bat-handled toddler spoon and fork set
- A USB-charged silicone moon night light with no removable battery
- One pouch of unsweetened apple and pumpkin purée

**Choking flag:** safe for under 3; no hard sweets, no detachable pieces. **Est. cost:** US$30–40. **Assembly:** 15 minutes.

### 2. Preschool, ages 3 to 5: ghost detective

Preschoolers love a job. This basket hands them one: find the paper ghosts you hid around the house.

- A shatterproof plastic magnifying glass
- Six picture-clue cards you draw, each pointing to a hidden paper ghost
- A child's torch with a screwed-shut battery door
- A washable ghost-stamp and ink pad
- A drawstring bag for the "evidence"
- One fruit pouch or a small box of raisins

**Choking flag:** stamp heads and raisins are small; keep the basket away from any sibling under 3. **Est. cost:** US$20–30. **Assembly:** 25 minutes, most of it drawing the clues.

### 3. Early school, ages 6 to 8: trick-or-treat night kit

Children this age want to feel ready for the big walk. Everything here gets used on 31 October.

- A plain canvas tote and fabric markers, to design their own candy bag
- A reflective slap band for each wrist
- A kid-sized headlamp
- A street map you print, so they can plan the route with you
- One full-size chocolate bar, to eat after the walk

**Choking flag:** fine for this age; the headlamp holds coin batteries, so check the door needs a screwdriver. **Est. cost:** US$25–35. **Assembly:** 20 minutes.

### 4. Tween, ages 9 to 12: horror-lite movie night

The fastest way to lose a tween is a cartoon pumpkin. Go darker in colour, not in content.

- A rental of one PG-rated Halloween film they choose
- Popcorn kernels and two seasoning shakers
- A black beanie with a small embroidered skull
- An escape-room-in-an-envelope game rated 10+
- A ticket that says they pick the next family film

**Choking flag:** popcorn and small game parts; store away from under-4s. **Est. cost:** US$35–50. **Assembly:** 20 minutes.

### 5. Teen, ages 13 to 17: the sleepover host kit

Teens judge a gift by whether their friends can use it too. Build for the group.

- Four cups of instant ramen
- A large bag of their favourite crisps
- A card game for four or more players
- A pack of glow sticks for a lights-out game
- A bubble-tea or takeaway voucher
- A note saying the basket is for them and whoever they invite

**Choking flag:** not a concern at this age. **Est. cost:** US$40–60. **Assembly:** 15 minutes.

### 6. Sibling pair: two of everything, one thing to share

Siblings count. Make the counts equal even when the contents differ, and add one item that only works with two people. A 2025 study of [fairness expectations in 54 toddlers aged 18 months](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12662943), published in *Infancy*, found that toddlers who attended preschool reacted more strongly to unequal shares, while having siblings made no clear difference.

- Two identical baskets in two colours, five items each
- A walkie-talkie pair, one per child
- A matching glow-in-the-dark T-shirt for each
- Age-matched snacks: purée for the younger, chocolate for the older
- One family board game, labelled "for both"

**Choking flag:** if one child is under 3, put the older child's small parts in a lidded box. **Est. cost:** US$45–70. **Assembly:** 30 minutes.

### 7. Allergy-friendly, ages 3 and up: the no-food basket

When you do not know a child's allergies, leave food out entirely. Even a "safe" sweet can share a factory line.

- A watercolour set and a pad of thick paper
- A skeleton-print pair of gloves
- A reusable water bottle with a bat print
- A child-size bat-wing cape
- A coupon to choose the Halloween film
- A small pot of modelling dough, after checking the label for wheat

**Choking flag:** choose a hook-and-loop cape, not a neck tie. **Est. cost:** US$20–35. **Assembly:** 15 minutes.

## Boo basket for kids by age: cost and choking compared

Here the seven builds collapse into four bands, each with its choking flag and estimated cost. Costs are rounded estimates.

| Age band | Basket theme | Choking-safe for under 3? | Est. cost (US$) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 to 3 | Bath-night pumpkin | Yes, every item | 30–40 |
| 3 to 8 | Ghost detective; trick-or-treat night kit | No, keep from toddlers | 20–35 |
| 9 to 17 | Movie night; sleepover host kit | No, popcorn and game parts | 35–60 |
| Mixed | Sibling pair; no-food basket | Only with small parts boxed | 20–70 |

Only the toddler build is safe to leave in reach of a child under 3. In a house with a baby, that matters more than price.

## What 16 CFR 1501 covers, and what it leaves to you

The US small-parts rule is narrower than most parents assume. [16 CFR part 1501](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1501) applies to toys and articles intended for children under 3, and it does not apply to items meant solely for children 3 and older. Its exemption list, section 1501.3, includes children's clothing and accessories such as buttons, barrettes, books, crayons, modelling clay and paint sets.

That is exactly what boo baskets hold. Buttoned Halloween pyjamas and a bat hair clip sit outside the rule, so checking their size is your job.

The [Nemours KidsHealth guide to choosing safe toys](https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/safe-toys.html) says toy age labels reflect safety, not intelligence, so a bright 2-year-old still gets the under-3 basket. It also says crayons and paints should carry "ASTM D-4236", and that old hand-me-down toys may miss current standards.

## How to boo a neighbour's kids: 5 rules

Boo-ing means leaving a basket on a doorstep in secret. With children who are not yours, it needs more care.

- **Ask a parent first.** A quick message also tells you whether the family celebrates Halloween.
- **Ask about allergies, or go food-free.** Use build 7 if the answer is unclear.
- **Leave it on the porch, not on the step.** Put it where a toddler at the door cannot reach it first.
- **No knock-and-run on a busy road.** On a street with traffic, text the parent instead of knocking.
- **Sign it.** Add your house number, so the family knows the gift came from a neighbour.

For a whole class, paper notes beat 25 baskets. Many schools have allergy policies that rule out shared food.

## What a 42-child study says about a polite "thank you"

Do not read a tween's thank-you as proof the basket landed. A 2023 [study of 42 Yucatec Maya children aged 6 and 10](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10751280), published in *Affective Science*, handed each child a broken version of their least-wanted toy in a "disappointing gift" task. The children largely followed their culture's rule of hiding negative feelings, and the 10-year-olds did so more than the 6-year-olds.

It was one culture, so it proves nothing universal. It does suggest older children manage their faces, which is why builds 4 and 5 let the child choose the film, the voucher and the guests.

## A Kids-mode Halloween page for the note, and 2 cases to skip it

A far-away grandparent or aunt can send the note as a link: switch the [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) to its Kids setting and the ghosts turn round and blushing, with zero blood, gore or jump scares. Trick throws confetti spiders, nothing goes black, and refusing just reads "maybe later?".

Your child knocks three times on a little haunted house, carves a pumpkin until its candle lights, and wipes fog from portraits to find up to six of your photos. In family mode, the closing question asks whether they will be your "favourite little pumpkin", and a Boo License card can be saved afterwards. Across all SubhSandesh pages, the average is 11.1 views per page, which suits a child who replays it.

When a grandparent's voice matters, pick the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium): it records a voice note of 60 seconds or less, and in kids mode there is no No button at all. A few tag lines work on the page or a paper tag:

- "A small ghost left this for the bravest pumpkin on the street."
- "No tricks inside. Only treats, and a torch for the walk."
- "Two of everything, so nobody has to count."

Skip the page when the family does not mark Halloween, or for a pre-reader who needs a paper card. Each page greets one child, so it cannot serve a class, and every screen is in English.

## Sources

- Meristo et al., toddler fairness expectations, *Infancy*, November 2025 (Europe PMC).
- Brady et al., Yucatec Maya children and a disappointing gift, *Affective Science*, December 2023 (Europe PMC).
- 16 CFR part 1501, current text on eCFR.
- Nemours KidsHealth, "Choosing Safe Toys", undated.
